newsitem.title: USA: Andrew remains positive for long term.
newsitem.headline: Andrew remains positive for long term.

text.p: Andrew Corp, which reported lower fiscal 1997 third quarter earnings and orders, said Wednesday it remains positive about its long term outlook.

"We were disappointed with the lack of order growth in the June quarter, but remain positive about our long-term market opportunities and our ability to excel in the global market," said Floyd English, chairman, president and chief executive officer, in a news release.

Earlier the company reported sales from continuing operations for its fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 1997 rose 10 percent from the same period a year ago to $208.9 million, while orders declined five percent from last year.

English said the company continued to see significant strength in its core markets, but third quarter orders declined from last year's levels due mainly to sluggishness in the U.S. personal communications services (PCS) market and weakness in the European cellular accessories market.
Net income for the quarter was $7.7 million or $0.08 per share including a restructuring charge of $0.04 per share and a charge for discontinued operations of $0.19 per share.

The charges cover costs of exiting certain businesses which have not met revenue and profit expectations. Andrew discontinued a network products business. It is also restructuring its European wireless products business and phasing-out of its fiber optic sensors and global messaging development activities.
Shares of Andrew fell 5-5/8 to 27-3/8 on turnover of about 9.8 million shares.
